_HOW_TO_ADD: EVENTS — add to scaffoldEvents, any order; they sort by year.
CHAPTERS — add/edit/delete entries in chapterDefs below. Each needs an id,
title, year, and either "captions" (exact caption strings from photos.json)
or both. Delete a chapter by removing its entry — its curated output is
pruned automatically on the next build.
PLACES — "places" maps a caption to [lat, lng] for the map. A caption with
no entry here simply gets no pin.
LEARNINGS — "learnings" is keyed by chapter or achievement id, so it survives
"approx": true renders a year as 'c. 2005' instead of claiming precision.

scaffoldEvents.title: Born in Qionghai
scaffoldEvents.detail: Hainan, China. An island province in the South China Sea.

scaffoldEvents.title: Kindergarten
scaffoldEvents.detail: Announcing the weather, and occasional updates, on the radio.

scaffoldEvents.title: Participated in the elementary school speech competition
scaffoldEvents.detail: A teacher advised me not to sing. That was the first time I learned I was probably tone-deaf.

learning.text: A teacher told me I couldn't sing, and I think I still might be tone deaf to this day. I have remembered that sentence for twenty years, which probably says more about how long an offhand remark from a teacher lasts than it does about my voice.

scaffoldEvents.title: The family moved to New York
scaffoldEvents.detail: Moved down from 3rd grade to 2nd grade because I could not speak English.
scaffoldEvents.linkLabel: A New Place — read the poem

learning.text: That was the first time I saw my dad let down a tear. I knew he was worried about me — but in that moment I also knew he was scared of this place, just like I was. Whoever reads this: the adults moving you are frightened too. They just do it anyway.

scaffoldEvents.title: Told my first-grade teacher I was going to America
scaffoldEvents.detail: In first grade I told my teacher I was going to America — a decision I couldn't quite understand at the time.
scaffoldEvents.linkLabel: A New Place — read the poem
scaffoldEvents.railText: In first grade I told my teacher I was going to America, a decision I couldn't quite understand.

scaffoldEvents.railText: First time being paid to do something I love.

scaffoldEvents.title: Started at Stuyvesant
scaffoldEvents.detail: Surrounded by the brightest of NYC.

learning.text: Being surrounded by people who are genuinely exceptional at one thing is humbling, and the wrong lesson to take from it is to go find your one thing and grind. The right one — the one it took me years to act on — is that you need to be good at more than one thing to excel. The overlap is where you're actually rare.

scaffoldEvents.title: Graduated Stuyvesant
scaffoldEvents.detail: Four years at Stuyvesant, then a year at Stony Brook to earn the transfer.

scaffoldEvents.title: Stony Brook University
scaffoldEvents.detail: The year between. Head down on the requirement classes and the GPA needed to secure the guaranteed transfer to Cornell.

scaffoldEvents.title: Cornell, on a guaranteed transfer
scaffoldEvents.detail: September 2018. B.S. Information Science. Joined clubs and organizations; made lifelong connections.

learning.text: Stuyvesant taught me there were more talented people than I'd assumed. Cornell taught me the same lesson one level up — more intelligent, harder-working, and no end to it. At some point you stop measuring yourself against the room and start looking for the people you want to keep.

scaffoldEvents.title: Collegiate table tennis
scaffoldEvents.detail: Played on the team. If only college pickleball had been a thing back then.

scaffoldEvents.title: Lockdown, alone on campus
scaffoldEvents.detail: The lockdown came out of nowhere. I stayed at Cornell because it was safer than home in NYC, and had the whole campus to myself.

learning.text: I had an empty Cornell campus to myself for months and almost no record of it. I wish I had taken the photos and flown the drone. What I did find was running, which I still have — so the year wasn't empty, it just left less behind than it should have. Document the strange stretches while you are inside them.

scaffoldEvents.title: Moved to Seattle
scaffoldEvents.detail: June 2021, for a job at Amazon. Started in inbound sales.

learning.text: Moving across the country to a city where I knew almost no one is the thing I would have called the risky choice at the time. It is where I got comfortable in my own skin, professionally and otherwise. The confidence did not come from the job — it came from having to build a life from nothing in particular.

scaffoldEvents.title: Family trip to visit home, Taiwan, Hong Kong and Thailand
scaffoldEvents.detail: First family trip — learned to tolerate each other more, and began to enjoy travelling the world.

achievements.title: Inbound sales → AWS, games and betting
achievements.detail: Started in inbound sales at Amazon, moved to AWS selling into the games industry, then into betting and gaming specifically. Through 2024.

achievements.title: Program Manager — Amazon Business
achievements.detail: March 2024. A new role, a new foundation, a different skillset from sales.

learning.text: Changing discipline three years in means being a beginner again on purpose, in front of people who watched you be competent at something else. That trade is almost always worth it, and it never once feels like it in the first six months.

achievements.title: Competing at 5.0
achievements.detail: January 2025 — started playing pickleball tournaments competitively. Won a few local ones. Met a lot of people along the way and built a community.

learning.text: I went in for the competition and what I actually got was a community. The tournaments are the excuse; the people you keep showing up with are the thing. If you are deciding whether to enter — enter, and not for the result.

achievements.title: Stacked
achievements.detail: A doubles-matching system built on complementary fit rather than similarity.

_achievements_note: No 'included' or 'why' set — the model decides which are defining moments and which are résumé lines, and argues each call.
_letters_NEEDS_YOU: Who would you write to, and when should it reach them? Even one real letter carries the whole product.
_traditions_NEEDS_YOU: One thing your family always does, described as if to someone who has never seen it — plus the part nobody else knows. Something that survived the move from Hainan is the obvious place to look.

quotes.text: In first grade I told my teacher I was going to America, a decision I couldn't quite understand.
Forty thousand feet above ground, I pondered on the cold seat as I leaned on mom's shoulder. I knew she was excited. But I was afraid.
That was the first time I saw dad let down a tear. I knew he was worried about me. But in that moment, I also knew that he was scared of this place just like I was.

noAnswer.why: He never wrote about this. The archive returns nothing rather than inferring an answer — a plausible reconstruction of what someone would have said is the one output this product will not produce.

_learnings_NEEDS_YOU: Five trip chapters still have none. kind is 'advice', 'reflection', or 'forward'.
